decisions.option: A (one pub and bank change: decimal comma read, thousands form refused in the entry box with the given note, hints say whole number)
decisions.what_changed: Grammar (pub web/src/tasks/quant/numeric.ts, bank hb.gen.quant.entry, same in both): digits, one comma, then one or two digits is a decimal comma ('3,5' = 3.5, '0,25' = 0.25, '-1,5' = -1.5, also with sign, '$' and '%' as before; ',5', '3,', '3,14159', '1,5,0' stay unreadable). Two readers of one grammar: parseEntry / parse_entry (scoring) still reads the thousands form d,ddd ('1,500' = 1500, '12,345.5', '0,500' = 500) exactly as before, because results are always re-scored from raw responses (section 7.8) and the old entry box accepted and stored such answers; checkNewEntry / check_new_entry (new, the entry box's check) returns 'ok' | 'thousands' | 'unreadable' and refuses the thousands form. isThousandsEntry / is_thousands_entry is the shared predicate. Why old saves re-score unchanged: the decimal-comma pattern is disjoint from every form the old grammar read (it needs 1-2 digits after the comma, the thousands form exactly 3), so for every string the old parser read the new one returns the same value (property-tested against a frozen verbatim copy of the old parser, fast-check and hypothesis), and the only strings read now and not before are decimal commas, which the old box refused, so no stored response can contain one; time-outs store null. Entry box (NumericEntry.svelte): the prop accepts:(text)=>boolean became check:(text)=>EntryVerdict ('ok' | 'format' | 'thousands'); 'thousands' shows THOUSANDS_NOTE (entry-copy.ts) with aria-invalid, the entry is not submitted and typing clears the note, like the UX-024 notes. QuantRenderer maps checkNewEntry plus its whole-number rule onto that verdict ('3,5' on a whole-number item is 3.5, so it gets the whole-number note; '35,0' is 35 and goes through). SeriesRenderer only adapts to the new prop: its own grammar and notes are unchanged ('1,500' and '3,5' get the whole-number note there, as before). Hints: quant HINTS (templates.ts) and the bank twin spec.HINTS now say 'whole number' and equal the entry box's FORMAT_HINTS for all three formats (series already said whole number; no series string changed). Generator version and item ids: the hint is part of every generated quant spec, and family.ts says to bump generatorVersion whenever generate output changes. A bump (1.3.0 -> 1.4.0, bank 1.4.0+py) would make resolveItem (exact version match, A18) return null for every saved i:quant:1.3.0:<seed> id, so registryObservation skips each saved quant answer as 'unresolved' and QR drops out of local re-scoring of every existing save (M1 has no server or kept payload). So the version stays 1.3.0 and only the display hint changes in place, in both twins and the TS dump: I regenerated golden/ts_dumps/quant.json (npm run dump:families -- --family quant --n 1000 --bank) and compared it with the previous copy, 1000 of 1000 items identical in every field except spec.hint (958 hint lines changed, the 42 decimal items unchanged). The bank twin keeps 1.3.0+py, its verifier's hint_matches check passes on the new dump, and no stored record anywhere (bank items/, panels/, pub fixtures, supabase) carries the old hint text. A new pub test (hints.test.ts) pins it: ids i:quant:1.3.0:saved-0..299 resolve through resolveItem, and a structuralHash of their content without spec.hint is pinned (2b07f5d0355e), so any change to what a 1.3.0 item is fails until the version moves. This deviates from the literal family.ts wording; see requests and spec_out_of_step. Shared vectors: web/src/tasks/quant/entry-vectors.ts (85 hand-written cases: raw, value, before = the old grammar's value, new_entry) serialised to bank golden/ts_dumps/quant_entry.json, a new parity file listed in ts-dumps-sync.test.ts PARITY_FILES with its own staleness check; the bank's tests/gen/test_quant_entry.py checks parse_entry, check_new_entry and the frozen old parser against every case.

The NumericEntry prop changed from accepts:(text)=>boolean to check:(text)=>EntryVerdict (both renderers updated; no other users).
open_issues: Series keeps its own integer grammar: '1,500' there gets the whole-number note ('...with no spaces or commas...'), not the thousands note. If the same note is wanted in series, SeriesRenderer's check can return 'thousands' for a d,ddd entry (one line).

normalize-digits.ts compacts spaces only in a plain number with a point, so a space-grouped decimal comma ('1 000,5') is still refused with the format note; extending the compaction to a comma would read it as 1000.5 (normalize-digits.test.ts pins today's behaviour). Left as is.

FORMAT_NOTES.decimal still says 'a point (.) for decimals, with no spaces or commas'. It is still correct advice, since the point is the asked form, but a comma decimal is now read too. Left unchanged (pinned in quant.dom.test.ts).

Fermi has its own magnitude grammar with the opposite convention (commas group thousands as in 31,557,600; a decimal comma is refused). It does not share this grammar and was not changed; the owner may want one convention across boxes.

Bank consumers of parse_entry outside scoring (hb.verify.solvers _entry_candidate, hb.verify.answers _number) now also read a decimal comma. A grep of panels/ and items/ found no answer or value of the d,dd form, so no recorded verdict changes when recomputed.

requests: owner of web/src/tasks/family.ts (Versions rule) and ids.ts/registry.ts docs: add that display-only copy no scoring, selection or verification reads apart from its own equality check (quant spec.hint) may change at the same generator version when every other field is byte-identical for every seed (checked by comparing the dumps), because a bump makes resolveItem drop every saved answer of the family from local re-scoring. If the owner prefers the literal rule instead, bump quant to 1.4.0 (bank 1.4.0+py), regenerate the dump, and update the SAVED_VERSION/digest pin in hints.test.ts; saved 1.3.0 quant answers would then be skipped as 'unresolved'.
